long_biography.plain_text:
During his first visit to Las Vegas in 1969, gambling entrepreneur Kazuo Okada brought back an old slot machine to dismantle and study. His interest in engineering later extended to the construction of Okada Manila, where he examined details from car parking to lighting and plumbing.

He also established a public setting for his interest in East Asian art, opening the Okada Museum of Art in Hakone in 2013. Its displays bring together Japanese, Chinese and Korean works. The museum encompasses painting and ceramics alongside calligraphy, lacquerware and religious sculpture, with works ranging from antiquity to the modern era.
long_biography.html:
During his first visit to Las Vegas in 1969, gambling entrepreneur Kazuo Okada brought back an old slot machine to dismantle and study. His interest in engineering later extended to the construction of Okada Manila, where he examined details from car parking to lighting and plumbing.

He also established a public setting for his interest in East Asian art, opening the Okada Museum of Art in Hakone in 2013. Its displays bring together Japanese, Chinese and Korean works. The museum encompasses painting and ceramics alongside calligraphy, lacquerware and religious sculpture, with works ranging from antiquity to the modern era.
